title: PagerDuty brieflet generator: synthesize telemetry snippets for Slack and PD attachments
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Problem: On-call responders often need a concise, contextualized summary pulled from traces, metrics, and logs when an alert fires. Currently responders must click through multiple dashboards and trace links which increases time-to-detect and time-to-ack.

Goal: Build a service that, given an alert/incident reference (PD incident or Slack thread), synthesizes a one-page 'brieflet' containing: top correlated traces, highest-frequency error fingerprints, a latency histogram snapshot, top relevant logs, and quick links to the full trace and dashboard. The brieflet should be attachable to PagerDuty incidents and Slack threads as a compact runbook seed for the responder and auto-populated into postmortems.

Design summary:
- "telemetry-extractor" service will accept an incident context (alert ID, time window, affected route/model) and run a prioritized pipeline: 1) query metrics for latency/error spikes; 2) run span aggregation to find top spans and error fingerprints; 3) pull top-of-window logs correlated by trace ID and sampling heuristics; 4) render a JSON brieflet and a small HTML/Markdown attachment for Slack/PD.
- Brieflet contents: title, summary sentence (computed via template + top metric delta), latency histogram PNG data URI, top 3 traces (link + short summary), top 5 log lines with timestamps, error fingerprints with counts, suggested runbook steps (templated), and links to dashboards/PRs.
- Privacy/KMS: strip any PII from logs by applying the existing redact pipeline; if redact flags present, note them on the brieflet. Storage: brieflets are ephemeral (TTL 7 days) in S3 with envelope encryption via KMS.
- Performance: target generation latency <= 6s for 1h windows and <= 12s for 24h windows for typical incidents. Use precomputed metric aggregates where available to reduce query time.

Acceptance criteria:
- When a PD incident triggers, the PD webhook can request a brieflet and receive a JSON payload + attachment URL within SLA (<=10s median).
- Slack threads can attach the brieflet into the conversation via the Ops bot with a compact Markdown summary and expand link.
- Brieflets include at least one correlated trace and one high-frequency error fingerprint when present in the window.
- Redaction is applied and flagged when log lines contain PII-like patterns.
- End-to-end integration test exists: synthetic alert -> brieflet generation -> PD incident attach -> Slack bot post.

Implementation steps:
1) Build telemetry-extractor service (Go) exposing a /brieflet endpoint.
2) Implement prioritized query planner to choose metric/trace/log queries based on alert type and time window.
3) Integrate existing redact pipeline and KMS envelope encryption for S3 storage.
4) Add PD webhook handler and Slack Ops-bot action to attach brieflets.
5) Create console toggle and RBAC to control who can request brieflets.
6) Add observability dashboards for brieflet generation latency and error rates.

Trade-offs & open questions:
- Sampling: full trace retrieval is expensive; we need a heuristic to pick representative traces (by error count, latency, or request volume).
- Storage TTL: 7 days is a compromise between auditability and storage cost. Ops may want longer retention for postmortems.
- PII detection accuracy vs recall: aggressive redaction may remove useful context. We will start with conservative regex + allow opt-in fuller logs for enterprise tenants.
